items.title: Nat Hentoff interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 12, 2007
items.q: He did Faulkner, he did Conrad Aiken.

ctx.x: It was fantastic and the look on her face, you know the way she’s just groovin’ to what he’s playing. And I’m thinking like it must have been a wonderful moment but also sort of anxious, like, are the cameras working? Are we getting that?

Oh Herridge did all kinds of stuff on television. He did Faulkner, he did Conrad Aiken. He had his own free-form thing. And before we did that show he had picked out, he knew, he was at CBS a long time, he picked out cameramen and women who could improvise. He said don’t worry about being in the shot, that doesn’t count. The studio is the studio. There’s no set. And never mind what you hear from the control room. If you get a shot, use it. And that’s why we have some of the shots in there, like Basie listening to…
Aw, gee. You think Lester just kind of ran out of gas?
